# Quickstart

Criterium is a benchmarking library for Clojure that provides statistically
rigorous timing measurements. Unlike simple timing with `(time ...)`,
criterium accounts for JVM warmup, measures many samples, and reports
statistical summaries.


## Your First Benchmark

The `bench` macro is the main entry point. Pass it any expression:


::: {.sourceClojure}
```clojure
(bench/bench (reduce + [1 2]))
```
:::



::: {.sourceClojure}
```clojure

:::


That's it. Criterium automatically:


- Warms up the JIT compiler so you measure optimized code
- Runs your expression thousands of times
- Computes statistics from the samples
- Detects and reports outliers
- Detects and reports multimodal distributions of execution time
- Detects measurement problems caused by external load, turbo boost, etc


## Reading the Output

The output has three main sections. Here's what each means:

**Sample Scheme**

```
Sample Scheme: 200 samples with batch-size 10000 (2000000 evaluations)
```


- `200 samples` — number of timing measurements taken
- `batch-size 10000` — executions per sample (batched for timer resolution)
- `2000000 evaluations` — total executions during measurement

** Metric Statistics**

The numbers below illustrate the output format only; the magnitudes are
not a current measurement.

```
  Elapsed Time median: 3.90 ns CI [3.88 3.92] (0.025 0.975)
  Elapsed Time spread: [3.76 4.10] ns (10th-90th percentile)
Elapsed Time extremes: [3.76 4.10] ns
```

Criterium takes the measured samples and bootstraps statistics.  The reported
values are the median, the mean and the spread.  The median includes a 95%
confidence interval for the statistic.  The spread show the bootstrapped p10
and p90 values.

::: {.callout-note}
The default output relies mainly on parametric free,
distribution free statistics.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
The statistics are bootstrapped to get most accuracy out of limited samples
and to get confidence intervals.
:::
```

**Outliers**

```
Outliers (outliers / samples): low-severe 0 (0.0%), low-mild 1 (0.5%), ...
```

Outliers are samples far from the typical range. A few high outliers are
normal (GC pauses, OS scheduling). Many outliers suggest unstable
measurements.



## Benchmarking with Data

When benchmarking code that uses data, you'll often define the data
outside the benchmark. Criterium handles this correctly:


::: {.sourceClojure}
```clojure
(let [data (vec (range 1000))]
  (bench/bench (reduce + data)))
```
:::



::: {.callout-note}
## OUT
```
                       Sample Scheme: 200 samples with batch-size 4 (800 evaluations)
                 Elapsed Time median: 4.26 µs CI [4.26 4.26] (0.025 0.975)
                 Elapsed Time spread: [3.97 4.50] µs (10th-90th percentile)
               Elapsed Time extremes: [3.85 4.83] µs
               Elapsed Time skewness: 0.2965 (slightly right-skewed)
                            kurtosis: 0.2008 (light tails (platykurtic))
                                  CV: 0.0478 (low variability)
                        Elapsed Time: Found 14 outliers in 200 samples (7.00 %) [medcouple-adjusted boxplot]
                                         low-mild	 2 (1.0000 %)
                                        high-mild	 1 (0.5000 %)
                                      high-severe	 11 (5.5000 %)
                        Elapsed Time: medcouple 0.0579 (slightly right-skewed)

                        Elapsed Time: Sample Independence Classification
               Lag-1 autocorrelation: 0.01 (none)
                   Ljung-Box p-value: 0.61
                          Assessment: Warning
                             Pattern: Periodic structure detected
                    Suspected period: 44 samples (r=0.35, moderate)
                      Recommendation: Investigate GC logs; increase heap

                        Elapsed Time: Effective Sample Size
 Lag-1 autocorrelation (no outliers): 0.12 (none)
               Effective sample size: 147 of 186 (79%)
                 CI inflation factor: 1.12×
                        Elapsed Time: ACF Plot (n=200):
                                      Lag   ACF
                                       44    0.35                 |███████████████ (moderate)

                                      Thresholds: other [minor 0.15, moderate 0.25]

```
:::



::: {.printedClojure}
```clojure
499500

```
:::


The `data` binding is captured before timing begins. Only the `reduce`
call is measured, not the vector creation.

Each captured argument value is stored once, before timing, and then read
opaquely on every timed iteration. The read keeps the work in the loop:
the JIT can not prove the input is stable, so it can not hoist the measured
expression out of the loop or fold a `final` field read to a constant. The
setup (here the vector creation) still happens once, before timing.

Here's a clearer example showing what gets measured:


::: {.sourceClojure}
```clojure
(let [expensive-setup (vec (range 10000))] (bench/bench (first expensive-setup)))
```
:::



::: {.sourceClojure}
```clojure
                       Sample Scheme: 200 samples with batch-size 1250 (250000 evaluations)
                 Elapsed Time median: 11.2 ns CI [11.2 11.2] (0.025 0.975)
                 Elapsed Time spread: [10.9 11.7] ns (10th-90th percentile)
               Elapsed Time extremes: [10.8 13.1] ns
               Elapsed Time skewness: 1.8517 (strongly right-skewed)
                            kurtosis: 4.7013 (heavy tails (leptokurtic))
                                  CV: 0.0353 (low variability)
                        Elapsed Time: Found 19 outliers in 200 samples (9.50 %) [medcouple-adjusted boxplot]
                                         low-mild	 2 (1.0000 %)
                                        high-mild	 12 (6.0000 %)
                                      high-severe	 5 (2.5000 %)
                        Elapsed Time: medcouple 0.2871 (moderately right-skewed)

                        Elapsed Time: Sample Independence Classification
               Lag-1 autocorrelation: 0.04 (none)
                   Ljung-Box p-value: 0.92
                          Assessment: Acceptable

                        Elapsed Time: Effective Sample Size
 Lag-1 autocorrelation (no outliers): 0.35 (moderate)
               Effective sample size: 88 of 181 (49%)
                 CI inflation factor: 1.44×

```
:::


Only this is timed

The 10,000-element vector is created once. The benchmark measures only
the `first` call, which takes nanoseconds regardless of the setup cost.
